newsitem.title: UK: Europe oil firms face huge clean-up bill - paper.
newsitem.headline: Europe oil firms face huge clean-up bill - paper.

text.p: European oil companies face a bill of at least 13.6 billion sterling ($22.7 billion) for disposing of off-shore rigs and platforms, according to a confidential report commissioned for the European Union (EU), the Guardian newspaper said Wednesday.
The report, for the EU's environment and energy directives, gives details about more than 1,600 off-shore installations, most of which will end their life within 30 years, the paper reported.
Estimates in the report put costs at 13.6 billion sterling for removing steel structures alone, excluding concrete base substructures and the removal of floating production facilities.

Such reports are often used as a prelude to the European Commission preparing legislation. Difficulties for the exploration and production companies would increase if the EU decided it were politically expedient to legislate to limit the disposal methods companies are allowed to use.
